title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional backoff thrashing
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Fix: Stabilize SLO enforcer backoff logic to prevent regional thrashing under partial outage; improves region affinity and adds jitter.
body:
Context: During a recent partial region outage (SUP-3344) the SLO enforcer entered a backoff loop that caused repeated regional failovers (thrashing) for a subset of customers. Root cause was a combination of a global backoff counter and deterministic backoff intervals that synchronized across controllers, plus an aggressive immediate failover path that did not respect per-region cooldown. This PR is a hotfix to stabilize the enforcer and prevent oscillation while preserving fast failover for severe region-level failures.

What I changed (summary):
- Introduced per-region token-bucket based backoff state so each region's enforcer has independent cooldown windows (services/slo-enforcer/backoff.go).
- Added randomized jitter to backoff intervals to avoid synchronization across replicas.
- Tightened the regional affinity check: prefer sticky region when latency is within SLO, only allow failover when region is clearly degraded for the configured SLO window (pkg/routing/region_affinity.go).
- Reduced aggressiveness of immediate remote failover path; now requires two consecutive SLO violations or a severity override from the global controller.
- Added unit and integration tests that reproduce thrashing pattern and assert stability under noisy partial outages (services/slo-enforcer/backoff_test.go, perf-canary integration harness).
- Small docs and helm defaults update with rollout guidance and new knobs (docs/operational/slo-enforcer.md, helm/redwood/values-slo.yaml).

Why this is safe as a hotfix: Changes are localized to the SLO enforcer path, default behavior is conservative (adds jitter, separates state), and rollout plan uses canary on Dedicated clusters before global rollout. We added tests and a short perf-canary scenario to validate behavior under simulated flapping.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover token-bucket semantics, jitter distribution bounds, and the dual-violation requirement for immediate failover.
- Integration test (perf-canary) simulates 20% transient latency increase in primary region and verifies no cross-region thrash for 5 consecutive cycles.
- Ran end-to-end on staging Dedicated cluster for 6 hours; observed stable region affinity and significantly fewer regional failovers in the trace.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge hotfix to main (this PR).
2) Canary deploy to ten Dedicated clusters for 24h. Monitor: slo-enforcer errors, regional-failover-count, and customer-facing latency SLOs.
3) If stable, promote to all Dedicated clusters; then schedule a controlled rollout for hosted regions (48h window).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration perf-canary scenario added
- [x] Staging validation completed
- [x] Docs updated with guidance and knobs
- [x] CI green on rerun (initial CI had a flaky test that was fixed)

Notes: This PR deliberately avoids changing SLA semantics or default thresholds; it reduces the coupling that led to synchronized backoff and adds operational knobs for SRE to tune cooldown windows. Related: ENG-8421 tracks a follow-up to expose region cooldown metrics and per-customer tuning.
